title: Latency causality sketchpad — perf sync 2026-04-02
content:
Attendees: Priya (notes), Ethan, María, Liam, +1 (shadow runner)
Context: quick sync after yesterday's shadow-run that showed an intermittent p99 spike for redwood-7B-v1 on h100-pool-2. This doc is a rough sketch of hypotheses, immediate mitigations, and reproducibility steps. Intention is to capture the thread-of-thought rather than a polished postmortem.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Observed: p50 stable (~45ms), p95 ~120ms, p99 jumped from ~220ms baseline to ~640ms for ~3m window during mixed-seq shadow-run at 600 qps.
- Likely surface causes: KV-cache eviction storm + sequencer priming + rare kernel path on mixed-quantized layers.
- Next immediate actions: reproduce in isolated lab (bench-runner v2), collect full perf traces (perf-collector v1.4), instrument kvcache counters and sequencer staging.

Raw observations from run 2026-04-01T23:40Z (shadow-run id bench-312):
- Model: redwood-7B-v1, seq_len avg: 256, mixed payloads 16% long-context (>1024) requests.
- HW: h100-pool-2 (4xH100 per node), 48 workers in shadow.
- Traffic shape: Poisson arrival, bursty at minute boundaries because of client batching (investigate client-side prep).
- Metrics snapshot: p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=640ms (window 23:42:00 - 23:45:00). GPU util dipped from 72% to 38% during spike window.
- KV-cache hit rate dropped from 83% -> 27% for requests with common prefixes.
- Sequencer length queue spiked (observer metric sequencer.pending_len) to 1800 from nominal 120.
- Traces show worker-side backpressure edges: worker-17 had a 2s stall waiting on I/O for cache load (trace ids: trc-88a9, trc-88b0)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV-cache eviction storm: a set of long-context requests caused tons of KV cache entries to be loaded and then evicted, causing I/O thrash and serialization at the worker process when loading KV pages. Corroborated by hit-rate dive and I/O waits in traces.
2) Sequencer priming + head-of-line blocking: sequencer scheduling pushed large requests earlier and queueing of small requests behind them; when cache miss hit the front worker, queued small requests wait -> p99 increases.
3) Rare kernel fallback: for certain token lengths and quantization boundaries, a slower kernel path triggered (seen in cpu kernel time slices in traces) but this doesn't fully explain GPU util drop.
4) Client batching artifact: upstream client batched multiple short requests into simultaneous arrivals at minute boundary causing microbursts; this amplifies the above.

Immediate experiments to run (owner / ETA):
- E1: Reproduce with bench-runner v2 in isolated 8-node h100 lab with same request mix (script: bench/scripts/repro-mixedseq-2026-04-02.sh). Owner: Ethan. ETA: 2026-04-03 EOD.
- E2: Turn off KV-cache (config override) and rerun the shadow traffic to see p99 behavior (if KV-cache is culprit p99 should improve but overall cost might increase). Owner: María. ETA: 2026-04-03 morning.
- E3: Force deterministic sequencing (no priority) for a test run to see sequencer impact. Owner: Liam. ETA: 2026-04-03 morning.
- E4: Increase sequencer window and add prefetch for top N prefixes (instrumentation-only, no production change) in a canary cluster and capture traces. Owner: Priya (with SRE). ETA: 2026-04-04.

Instrumentation checklist (what to capture):
- KV-cache: per-key load latencies, eviction counts, memory pressure sampling.
- Sequencer: pending_len, per-priority latency, scheduling decisions (ids).
- Worker traces: syscalls blocked on file I/O, time in kernel fallback paths, GpuMemcpy timings.
- Network: client arrival timestamps and burst correlation; confirm if client-side batching aligns to minute boundary.
- Perf metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 per-model, qps, GPU util, context-switches.

Temporary mitigations discussed:
- Soft limit on long-context requests in shadow traffic (throttle 16% -> 6%) until repro done. (Action: Ethan to add throttling rule: bench/traffic-configs/mixedseq-throttle-v1).
- Short-term sequencer fallback policy: if pending_len > 800, spawn aux workers to drain (SRE runbook adjustment). (Action: Liam to draft runbook change).

Notes from quick trace read (María):
- Two workers exhibited similar I/O stalls; both colocated on node h100-03; suspect node-level filesystem contention (nvme tier). Check node metrics and firmware.
- There are correlated small gc spikes in the language-runner process that coincide with I/O waits — need heap profile.

Open questions / unresolved: 
- Did a deploy or config change precede 23:40Z? (Ops says no deploy; but a config rollout for cache TTL was scheduled earlier that day — confirm.)
- Are there known firmware anomalies for h100-03? (Infra pinged)
- Is client-side batching intentional or a side-effect of traffic generator? (Product/growth?)

Linked tickets / followups:
- JIRA-PERF-4321: investigate p99 regression (linked).
- github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/876: experimental KV eviction logging (review comments).
- bench run: internal-bench://runs/2026-04-02/bench-312 -> archived traces under s3://redwood-perf/bench-312/*.trace

Rough decision criteria (how we'll know):
- If E2 (disable kvcache) reduces p99 by >50% during synthetic microburst -> KV-cache is primary culprit.
- If forcing deterministic sequencing reduces pending_len and p99 without changing cache hit-rate -> Sequencer policy contributes significantly.
- If neither reproduces, escalate to kernel-engineering for a deeper kernel path inspection.

Action items (short):
- Ethan: repro script + run logs (2026-04-03 EOD).
- María: run E2, collect traces, get heap profile for language-runner (2026-04-03 AM).
- Liam: draft sequencer runbook change and run deterministic sequencing experiment (2026-04-03 AM).
- Priya: coordinate infra checks for h100-03 and collect node-level metrics (2026-04-02 night).

Notes to self / ephemeral thoughts:
- Might be worth adding a "cache-temperature" gauge in the metrics panel (hot vs cold key sets) — would make these events visible immediately.
- Consider adding a tiny randomized jitter in the sequencer enqueue to avoid alignment spikes (cheap, low-risk experiment).

Meeting adjourned 2026-04-02 09:15 PST. Next sync: quick standup tomorrow 09:00 PST if a repro is found, otherwise escalate channel updates.

Unpolished scratch links:
- bench run script: //bench/scripts/repro-mixedseq-2026-04-02.sh
- trace ids to dig: trc-88a9, trc-88b0, trc-88d3
- quick grep commands: 
  - grep -R "kv_evict" logs/bench-312 | head
  - jq '.metrics|{p50,p95,p99,qps}' bench-312/summary.json

If you pick up any of the actions, drop a quick comment here with status. This doc will be refined into a short incident note if we confirm root cause.
